transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-17
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Connor, Sofia Ramirez, Dr. Amir Khan, Nora Lee (Orchid Health)
Recording: (fireflies link)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Jordan Ellis from Redwood, I'll run the kickoff along with Priya and Maya. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Liam: Good, thanks. Excited to get started. We just wrapped internal prep and wanted to align on next steps.
[00:18] Maya: Quick agenda - security + infra, pilot scope & success metrics, bench runs, and rollout plan. We'll leave time for Q&A.
[00:28] Sofia: That works. We're particularly focused on PII handling and on-prem options for some workloads.
[00:34] Jordan: Totally. We'll cover our private deployment patterns and dedicated capacity as well as hosted API trade-offs.
[00:42] Priya: A couple of notes up front - when we talk about performance I'm going to refer to KV cache behavior and batching overhead. Also we usually present quantization recommendations after the first bench.
[00:51] Dr. Khan: Great. From a clinical perspective the main success criteria are accuracy of note generation, latency under 1s for interactive workflows, and strict data residency controls.
[01:05] Jordan: Noted. We'll capture that as part of the pilot success criteria.
[01:12] Nora: Security specifics - we need SOC 2 evidence, HSM/KMS integration guidance, SSO via SAML (Okta), and audit log export frequency. Also data retention defaults.
[01:25] Maya: We have a SOC2 pack and KMS integration doc, we'll share links post-call. Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM and retention is configurable; we'll send the defaults plus options.
[01:36] Jordan: For SSO we support SAML/OIDC, and RBAC can be mapped to your groups. We'll include role mapping examples.
[01:44] Sofia: Good, we also want to know about network topology for private deployments - do you do VPC peering or customer-managed VPN?
[01:52] Priya: Both patterns are supported. For private we usually deploy a control plane in our managed account but you can opt for a customer-managed VPC with peering or a transit VPN; on-prem air-gapped is possible but longer lead time.
[02:05] Liam: Cost question - we run a mix of interactive clinician tools and batch summarization jobs. How do we think about hosted vs dedicated?
[02:14] Jordan: Hosted is fastest to start and lower ops overhead. Dedicated (reserved) gives predictable throughput and isolation; private gives full network control. There's a cost tradeoff - dedicated reserved capacity reduces per-token unit cost for heavy steady workloads.
[02:28] Priya: For interactive, latency SLOs are critical - we can configure warm pools and KV cache to hit sub-second medians for short contexts. For batch jobs, you can use larger batch sizes and cheaper quantized variants.
[02:42] Sofia: Are there quantized model profiles you'd recommend for EHR text?
[02:47] Priya: We'll propose model + quantization profiles after we run the initial benchmark; generally int8-ish quant is good for throughput but check for any quality regressions.
[02:56] Dr. Khan: Quality regressions are non-negotiable for clinical notes - we need an eval set and automatic quality regression alerts.
[03:06] Maya: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring tied to prompt sets - we can instrument your evals and set alerts on any regression. We'll include an eval-run template.
[03:18] Jordan: Timeline proposal - week 0: infra setup and SSO; week 1-2: bench runs and model selection; week 3-4: pilot with 2-3 clinician users; week 5: review and decide next steps. Sound reasonable?
[03:33] Liam: That's aligned with what we discussed internally. We want pilot start no later than mid-February.
[03:40] Jordan: That gives us about 4 weeks, doable if we get the dev VPC and sample data quickly.
[03:47] Sofia: We'll prioritize prod-adjacent dev environment access. Who from your side will need console access?
[03:53] Maya: Priya and I will provision initial roles, but we'll need a list of Orchid users and their roles to map RBAC.
[04:01] Nora: Also clarify data deletion semantics - if we use hosted, what's retained?
[04:06] Jordan: By default hosted data retention is 30 days for logs and request payloads unless you opt-out; for Private you control retention. We'll share the exact retention matrix.
[04:16] Priya: For the bench, please provide a small anonymized sample (500,000 records) representing typical notes and a set of evaluation prompts. We recommend removing PHI but keep structure.
[04:29] Sofia: We can provide an anonymized slice by Friday.
[04:33] Priya: Great. For benchmarks we'll run latency/cost and a few quality evals against the candidate models. We'll produce a spreadsheet with token counts, p95 latency, and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:45] Liam: Will you be able to run the bench in our region? We need EU region for data residency for some customers.
[04:51] Priya: Yes, we have EU regions available. We'll specify which model variants run where.
[04:58] Dr. Khan: A question on audit and compliance - can we get immutable audit logs and daily exports?
[05:05] Maya: Yes, audit logs are immutable and we can push exports to your S3 or your SIEM on a schedule. We'll include recommended retention and export frequency.
[05:16] Nora: Encryption - how is data encrypted at rest and in transit, and integration with our HSM?
[05:22] Jordan: All data is TLS in transit. At rest we use customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private deployments; hosted supports your KMS via integrations for enterprise accounts. We'll provide the KMS runbook.
[05:35] Sofia: For the pilot we'll likely start hosted with VPC peering for network isolation, then move to dedicated or private depending on results.
[05:44] Priya: Sounds like a good plan to minimize lead time. We'll provide a migration path that preserves model versions and cache warming profiles.
[05:54] Liam: Ok, pilot scope - what are the minimum success metrics again?
[05:58] Maya: From notes earlier: accuracy/clinical validity (qual triage by clinicians), interactive latency median < 1s and p95 < 2s for short contexts, and no PII leakage incidents on evaluation.
[06:10] Dr. Khan: We'll provide an acceptance checklist with sample cases.
[06:15] Jordan: Perfect. Any blockers we should call out now?
[06:19] Sofia: The only blocker is access to a sanitized data slice and network permissions for our dev subnet. Otherwise timeline is clear.
[06:27] Priya: We'll send an infra checklist to make that easy - VPC CIDRs, allowed egress, service accounts.
[06:34] Jordan: I'll attach the onboarding playbook and the infra checklist to the follow-up.
[06:39] Liam: Pricing - can you share an estimate for pilot costs and for the dedicated capacity?
[06:45] Jordan: We'll send a pilot estimate based on expected token volume and a reference for reserved capacity pricing. For the pilot it's usually consumption-based; for dedicated we can provide monthly commit tiers.
[06:55] Liam: Cool. Also curious about competitors - we've heard from Anthropic and also looked at SageMaker endpoints for an in-house path. Thoughts?
[07:03] Jordan: Anthropic's Claude is strong for safety but pricing/latency profiles differ. SageMaker gives full control but you manage all ops. Redwood sits in between - we provide a managed runtime tuned for inference costs and predictable latency with enterprise controls.
[07:18] Sofia: That helps. Any recommended eval prompts for clinical notes?
[07:22] Priya: We'll share a prompt set for summarization, diagnosis extraction, and safe response heuristics. Also include edge cases to detect hallucination.
[07:32] Dr. Khan: Please include examples where we compare before/after clinician edits - that helps quantify assistive value.
[07:38] Maya: We'll include that in the eval template.
[07:44] Jordan: Ok let's recap - Jordan to share security pack, playbook, pricing ballpark; Priya to run bench and request sample data; Maya to set up console access and check-ins; Orchid to provide anonymized data slice and dev VPC access.
[07:59] Liam: Sounds good. Any final questions?
[08:02] Nora: One quick one - incident response: do you provide SOC/IR contacts and SLAs?
[08:08] Maya: Yes, enterprise packages include 24/7 incident contact and escalation path; we will include the SOC/IR contact sheet.
[08:16] Sofia: Thanks everyone. We'll prioritize the sample data and access.
[08:20] Jordan: Great, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the benchmark. Thanks all.
[08:25] [END]
